title: Runtime Harmony: Multi-GPU Coordinator with NCCL Staggering and Attention-aware Kernel Routing
creator: Aisha Kapoor
body:
Summary:
Implement a multi-GPU runtime coordinator that harmonizes tensor/pipeline parallel execution with staggered NCCL windows and attention-aware kernel routing to improve end-to-end latency and utilization during prefill and decode phases. This ticket covers design and a first-pass implementation that schedules prefill/kw-prefill, balances comm overlap, and adapts kernel selection based on runtime token distributions.

Motivation / Background:
- Current multi-GPU traces show underutilized compute during prefill when NCCL collectives block hotspots and during decode when attention kernel choices cause imbalanced per-stage runtimes.
- We need a coordinator that reasons across three axes: (1) token phase (prefill vs decode), (2) parallelism topology (tensor/pipeline mapping), and (3) comm/backpressure behavior to enable NCCL overlap without violating correctness or SLOs.

Goals / Acceptance Criteria:
1) Scheduler should reduce average 95th-percentile latency for mixed prefill/decode workloads by >= 12% in 8-GPU topology benchmarks (same model family used in current infra).
2) Achieve >= 18% improvement in GPU utilization during the prefill window by allowing comm/compute overlap via staggered NCCL windows and opportunistic KV-cache prefetching.
3) No regression on single-GPU throughput or correctness; all unit tests and end-to-end torchscript validation must pass.
4) Expose a runtime configuration flag (mgpu.coordinator.mode = "adaptive" | "staggered" | "legacy") and telemetry for "comm_overlap_efficiency" and per-stage imbalance metrics.

Design Notes / Trade-offs:
- Staggered NCCL windows: open short, overlapping collective windows across neighboring pipeline stages to allow asynchronous transfer while preserving ordering. Trade-off is complexity in orchestrator + slightly increased memory pressure for buffering.
- Attention-aware kernel routing: at scheduling time select kernels (e.g., tiled-attn vs fused-causal-attn) based on predicted per-batch sequence length distribution and KV-cache hit rate. This requires lightweight profiling and a small decision table in the conductor.
- Token-phase aware prefetch: during prefill we prioritize large contiguous prefill batches to maximize NCCL bandwidth; during decode we switch to low-latency routing and favor smaller batch coalescing to avoid tail latency amplification.
- Correctness: must ensure deterministic output for pinned model versions. Any adaptive fallback during capacity contention must be conservative and logged.

Implementation Plan:
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement coordinator skeleton, NCCL staggering driver, and attention-aware kernel selector. Add telemetry hooks and config flags. Integrate with existing conductor API. (Estimated 3 weeks)
- Phase 2 (follow-up ticket): autoscaler-aware policies + rollout canary to 10% of Dedicated clusters, add additional heuristics derived from closed-loop metrics.

Testing Strategy:
- Unit tests for coordinator state transitions and stall recovery.
- Microbench: 8xA100 topology replicate current prefill/decode benchmark suite; baseline compare (legacy) vs staggered/adaptive.
- E2E correctness: run internal evals with deterministic seeds and compare token streams to gold.
- Chaos: simulate delayed NCCL completion and verify graceful backoff and fallback to legacy mode.

Instrumentation / Observability:
- New metrics: mgpu.coordinator.mode, mgpu.stage.imbalance_ms, mgpu.comm_overlap_efficiency, mgpu.kernelselect.decisions (histogram).
- Logs: structured event when scheduler switches kernels or engages staggered windows.
- Dashboards: add a runtime-2.4 panel showing per-stage utilization and comm overlap efficiency for rollout monitoring.

Rollout Plan:
- Start with internal perf cluster (canary) and run 72-hour stability tests; compare 95th latency and cost per token.
- If pass, progressive rollout to Dedicated reserved pools with a 1-week observation window. Provide automatic rollback to legacy on error thresholds (errors/sec > baseline*3 or 95th latency regresses > 10%).

Open Questions / Risks:
- Memory amplification from buffering overlapping collectives on large sequence lengths (L>4096). Need to cap overlap windows and add backpressure.
- Interaction with existing prefill batching heuristics: we must avoid double coalescing that would increase latency during bursty traffic.
- Safety for private deployments: ensure defaults are conservative and expose all toggles behind admin flags.

Acceptance Tests (PR checklist):
- [ ] Conductor unit tests added and green.
- [ ] Bench harness shows target 12% p95 improvement on benchmark job mgpu-prefill-v2.
- [ ] Telemetry surfaced to Grafana panel and smoke dashboard passes.

updates: 2026-02-16 - Aisha: Kickoff meeting done with Serving, Runtime, and Platform teams. Agreed on telemetry surface and config key names.
2026-02-22 - Miguel: Prototype NCCL staggering driver implemented; initial microbench shows 9% p95 improvement in best-case runs. High memory during L=4096 noted.
2026-02-27 - Priya (Perf): Provided baseline harness results and suggested tighter overlap caps for long sequences. Added benchmark job mgpu-prefill-v2.
2026-03-04 - Miguel: Integrated attention-aware kernel table. Microbench: adaptive mode improved utilization by 20% but p95 improvement fluctuates with token distribution.
2026-03-08 - Code review: runtime/pull/2145 has comments about locking granularity and a potential deadlock when a stage is preempted; Miguel addressed with optimistic try-lock and backoff.
2026-03-10 - Aisha: Updated acceptance criteria to require 12% p95 improvement; scheduled Phase 2 follow-up to add autoscaler-aware policies.
